#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources (single-line):
#   -t05-00:00:00
#   -c10
#   --mem-per-cpu=10240
#   -G1
#   -J 3sl
#   --export=ALL

#flux: --job-name=3sl
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 10
#flux: --time-limit=120h

# Omitted Slurm option: -G1 (GPU request)
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=10240
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --export=ALL
# Flux does not have a portable directive identical to Slurm --export.
# Performance implication: environment differences could affect runtime behavior; export needed variables explicitly if required.

module load anaconda
conda activate ilab
export PYTHONPATH="/adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/tensorflow-caney"

# Slurm used srun -G1 -n1; under Flux, run within allocation.
flux run -n 1 -c 10 python /adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/senegal-lcluc-tensorflow/projects/land_cover/scripts/predict.py \
  -c /adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/senegal-lcluc-tensorflow/projects/land_cover/configs/20220620/land_cover_256_trees_srv.yaml

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`-G1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=10240`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM.
